newsitem.title: THAILAND: Four Thai property firms deny ECD defaults.
newsitem.headline: Four Thai property firms deny ECD defaults.

text.p: Four property companies on Wednesday said they did not face any financial problems that would force them to default on obligations related to their Euro-convertible debentures.

Juldis Develop Plc, Property Perfect Plc, Bangkok Land Plc, and Land and Houses Plc in statements to the stock exchange denied a local press report that they could not meet their ECD interest payments and that their trustees were being sued by investors.
Juldis said the company has not failed to honour obligations on its 10-year, $60 million ECD which will mature in December 2003, including annual payment on its 4.25 percent interest.

Property Perfect said its five-year, $35 million ECD is not due to mature until 2001 and its average annual sale revenue of four billion baht in the past three years meant it did not have any cashflow problems in repaying debt.
The company said its ECD, with no attached put option, would yield a net 3.25 percent amounting to $1.1 million.

Bangkok Land said it has not been informed by trustees that they were being sued for any payment default on its three ECD issues which have outstanding unconverted units worth $150 million and 450 Swiss francs.
Bangkok Land said its first ECD, with 50 million swiss francs of unconverted units, matures in December this year while two other issues expire in March 2001 and August 2003.
Land and Houses said 86 percent of its $60 million debenture has been converted to common shares, leaving an outstanding $8.18 million debt from the issue.
The company said its debenture, due to mature in April 2003, has no put option.
